text:
priya: heads up — getting a new spike of 503s for hosted inference across multiple endpoints, customers reporting timeouts and increased p50/p95. putting a triage thread up.

alex: seeing the spike on the edge gateway too. p50 jumped from 180ms -> 900ms around 12:43 UTC.

sam: ops-bot alert fired: `gateway_503_rate > 5% for 5m` and several support tickets landed. link: https://redwood/alerts/2345

maria: quick logs — gateway shows `upstream request timeout` and a rise in `conn reset by peer`. sampling logs now.

luis: any rollout around that time? I don't see any deploys in prod between 12:40–12:44. config rollout queue empty.

priya: customers mention both text generation and embeddings calls failing. could be shared infra (edge/gateway) or K8s node oom?

alex: running a small grep on proxy logs: ```
# tail -n 200 proxy.log | grep "504\|503" | head
2026-03-17T12:43:02Z gateway ERROR upstream timeout id=abc123 svc=hosted-inference route=/v1/generate
2026-03-17T12:43:08Z gateway WARN conn reset by peer id=abc124
```

maria: traced a few requests into runtime: batcher lag was high, backlog ~1200 requests, kv-cache hit ratio dropped. suspecting a KV cache eviction storm hitting GPU runtime hotpaths.

sam: can we scale the batcher/retry queues as an immediate mitigation? I can push a temporary scale policy to +30% capacity.

luis: adding a temporary route-level circuit-breaker to fallback to smaller model variant for low-latency paths. will roll at 12:50 UTC.

priya: thanks. support-bot, please queue a customer status update: "Investigating increased timeouts, mitigation in progress. Will update in 15m."

support-bot: queued message to impacted customers (ticket ids: #4521, #4523, #4527).

ops-bot: autoscaler action: increased pool hosted-runtime-1 by 3 replicas at 12:51:05Z.

alex: after autoscale and circuit-breaker, error rate dropped to ~1.2% and p95 fell back. charts: https://redwood/metrics/hosted/503-heatmap?s=12:40&t=13:00

maria: root cause hypothesis: KV cache warmup/eviction storm caused batcher latency to spike which cascaded to gateway timeouts. correlates with a background warmup job that restarted on some nodes at 12:42 (logs show warmup pod restarts).

luis: action item 1: pin warmup job to rolling restart schedule and add jitter, avoid simultaneous restarts — owner: luis — due: 2026-03-18

sam: action item 2: add a short-term guard on batcher queue size + alert at 20% above baseline — owner: sam — due: 2026-03-18

maria: action item 3: add KV cache warm-reload telemetry (eviction rates, miss storm detector) and dashboard tile — owner: maria — due: 2026-03-20

priya: action item 4: customer comms follow-up (postmortem summary + mitigations) — owner: priya/support — due: 2026-03-18

alex: quick repro steps for the postmortem: 1) simulate warmup pod rolling restart across 30% of runtime nodes 2) flood small requests to force batching pressure 3) observe batcher backlog and gateway 503 rate. I'll draft a reproducible script.

priya: good. please include exact log snippets and dashboards in the postmortem. also add checklist for Dedicated customers on fallback models.

luis: rolling follow-up: will throttle the warmup job next maintenance window and add exponential backoff to its init sequence.

sam: note — we should also consider adding a per-customer circuit-breaker on heavy concurrent short requests to prevent noisy tenants triggering global backpressure. raised RFC: https://redwood/rfcs/rfc-2026-noisy-tenant-protection

priya: agreed. final check: error rate stable and customers updated. closing war-room but keeping follow-ups on the incidents sprint. thanks team :thumbsup:

support-bot: closing incident thread — follow-ups recorded in ticket #4521.

(reacts: priya :thumbsup:, alex :heart:)
